Source distinctions and conflicts

  • Figure 2 caption and opening paragraph give 10/10.0 mM Ag+, but detailed n++ discussion and general plating recipe give 1.0 mM. Figure 3 separately gives 1.5 mM.
  • Figure 2d caption repeats n++-Si while body and comparison identify n-Si. Preserve body/caption distinction.
  • Figure 5 caption and body print mC/cm² for 1.6/3.6/8.3/18.7 and 222 per monolayer; Figures 7/9 explicitly print µC/cm². Do not silently normalize source charge units.
  • Equivalent monolayers are upper-bound charge-derived amounts assuming 100% efficiency, not measured planar-area fraction or exact shell thickness.
  • Four histograms and four listed pulse durations appear, although Figure 7 caption says five samples. Five random image fields per sample is a different count.
  • First histogram mean/sigma are 2.2/2.4 nm; body gives smallest height 2.4 and spread 2 nm. Largest histogram sigma 6.1 nm versus rounded body 6 nm.
  • Figure 8 actual ordinate is particle density, not captioned mean height. The height-distribution ±sigma wording cannot establish the density error-bar statistic.
  • Body nucleation-rate range uses cm−2 ms−1; summary uses cm−2 s−1 with rounded values. Both are retained as conflicting source statements.
  • Abstract, body and summary give different rounded initial/saturation ranges. Current-model N∞ is approximately an order of magnitude above microscopy density.
  • Body says no Ag before 2–3 ms while Figure 5 includes a 2 ms image; low-end object density is close to contamination background. No detection-corrected nucleus count is provided.
  • NC-AFM height is measured; tip-convolved width is not true diameter. Approximately spherical diameter-as-height rationale differs from the hemispherical height-as-radius model.
  • TEM 10–25 Å objects have unspecified pulse duration and were mechanically transferred. They are not a verified same-sample match to 2–20 nm AFM height populations.
  • Table 1 expected spacings and intensities are ICDD reference values, not measured specimen intensities. Printed 111 reference spacing is 2.32 Å and must not be silently repaired.
  • Aqueous instability paragraph names AgO; later phase test contrasts Ag0 with Ag2O. The metallic SAED assignment is retained without creating an oxide synthesis record.
  • Printed Equation 2 contains A and lacks the explicit F factor present in Equation 1. A is not defined numerically; exact reproduction of N∞ is not supported by note 43 alone.
  • Band edges were not measured. Barrier energies, depletion widths and geometric N fits are models; z = 1 and hemispherical morphology are assumptions.
  • Equation 3 discussion refers to Figure 8 predictions, but the model curves are in Figure 9.
  • Summary says nucleation ceases near 20 ms; body explicitly limits measurements to ≤30 ms and allows undetectably slow continued nucleation on longer times.
  • TEM method calls 200 keV an accelerating voltage. Preserve the beam setting with its printed energy unit rather than silently transcribing kV.
  • Figure 2 labels potential in V but numerical ticks and body potentials are in the hundreds of mV. Preserve original axis and use explicit body mV data for typed features.
  • Step-height ±0.4 Å lacks statistic; Figure 7 sigma denotes height spread; Figure 8 error-bar definition conflicts with its ordinate; Figure 9 ±sigma is height spread, not SEM.
  • Figure 5, Figure 7, TEM transfer, current transients and the 15-experiment three-day series are source contexts with unknown exact physical sample joins.
  • Plotted current density includes multiple Faradaic processes; no current efficiency or exact silver mass is established by total charge alone.
